title: John: the Word made flesh
note: Rebuilt on 2026-11-26 from the Bible Explorer film of the same slug. lines: John is the fourth of the four Gospels. It tells the same story as Matthew, Mark, and Luke from a different height.
It begins before the world was made. And soon comes the sentence the whole book hangs on.
The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us.

scripture.text: The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us.

lines: John is built with care. An opening poem. A first half built around signs. And a second half that slows almost to a stop: five chapters are given to one evening.
Then come the cross, the resurrection, and a closing scene by the lake.

scripture.text: Jesus knew that His hour had come

lines: John calls Jesus' miracles signs, because each one points beyond itself to who he is. The first half is built around seven of them.
Signs can start faith. But faith that only wants miracles is thin.

scripture.text: Jesus performed this, the first of His signs, at Cana in Galilee.

lines: Seven times Jesus says I am, and adds a picture. Bread. Light. A gate. A shepherd. Resurrection and life. The way. The true vine.
I am the bread of life.
Each one takes something people can't live without and says: this is what I am for you.

scripture.text: I am the bread of life.

lines: The verb believe comes ninety-eight times in John, and the noun faith never does. Believing is something you do: coming to Jesus, trusting him, staying with him.
And eternal life, in John, is life with God that begins now.

scripture.text: to those who believed in His name, He gave the right to become children of God

lines: The second half opens when Jesus knows his hour has come. He washes his disciples' feet and gives them a new command.
A new commandment I give you: Love one another.
In John, the glory of God is seen most clearly at the cross. Then come the empty tomb and the risen Jesus.

scripture.text: A new commandment I give you: Love one another.

lines: Start at chapter one and read slowly. The key chapters are one, three, six, eleven, thirteen, seventeen, and twenty.
One caution. When John speaks of the Jews, he usually means the Jerusalem authorities. Jesus and nearly everyone in the story are Jews.
John tells you plainly why he wrote.
These are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God.
